resolutions.researcher_notes: No public source names this specific numbered 'Haradh Khuff-Hawiyah 3' line as operating; status inferred from context. Saudipedia: the Hawiyah Gas Plant became operational in 2001 and processes sour gas from the al-Khuff reservoir, and continues as an active installation. MEED documents Aramco's operating Haradh/Hawiyah gas-pipeline programme (e.g. Haradh-Uthmaniyah gas line HDUG-1). The Khuff-gas feed from Haradh to the operating Hawiyah plant is therefore operating by context. gem.wiki's sole cite (OPEC ASB 2012 p.75) is a general statistical bulletin that does not list individual pipeline specs; the ASB link now returns an HTML block page. offshore-technology.com repeats GEM's identical 43km/30in figures and traces to GEM, so it does not count as independent corroboration.

Fuel=Gas is unambiguous and corroborated by two independent sources. Saudipedia: Hawiyah Gas Plant processes non-associated sour gas from the al-Khuff and al-Jawf reservoirs (Khuff is a gas reservoir; the line carries Khuff gas). MEED: describes the Aramco gas-pipeline network in the Haradh/Hawiyah area. Both confirm the line is a gas pipeline.

No independent public source states 43 km for this line. The 43 km / 27 mi figure appears only on gem.wiki (which cites OPEC ASB 2012 p.75, a general bulletin that does not list per-pipeline lengths) and on offshore-technology.com, whose data-insights profile reproduces GEM's identical figures and traces to GEM. Aramco, MEED and Saudipedia describe the broader Haradh/Hawiyah pipeline network but give no length for this specific numbered Khuff feed line. UNRESOLVED.

No independent public source states 30 in for this line. The 30-inch figure appears only on gem.wiki and its GEM-derived echo offshore-technology.com. MEED cites specific diameters for other Hawiyah-area lines (48-in inlet/outlet, 24-in and 28-in NGL lines) but none for this Khuff feed. UNRESOLVED.

Refs support Saudi Arabia and the Haradh (Khuff)->Hawiyah Gas Plant endpoints. CONTRADICTION FLAG: the staged EndState/Province='Makkah' is almost certainly wrong. The Hawiyah Gas Plant that processes Haradh Khuff gas sits in the Ghawar/Haradh area of the EASTERN Province (Saudipedia locates it with the Ghawar field on the Master Gas System), not the Makkah region. 'Makkah'/'Al Hawiyah' looks conflated with the separate Madrakah-Al Hawiyah gas pipeline near Taif in Makkah region. Country (Saudi Arabia) and the Haradh->Hawiyah endpoints are supportable; recommend a human correct EndState/Province from Makkah to Eastern Province before applying.

Owner=Saudi Aramco (100%) supported. Saudipedia: Saudi Aramco operates the Hawiyah Gas Plant as part of its Master Gas System. MEED: the Haradh/Hawiyah gas-pipeline programme is Saudi Aramco's. Aramco is the sole owner/operator of Saudi Arabia's domestic gas transmission infrastructure, so 100% is consistent though the two sources do not state an explicit ownership percentage (hence medium, not high).
